scope: These concise notes paraphrase the retained track-specific sources named with each entry. Most are Wikipedia accounts, sometimes reporting another critic or an artist’s explanation; they are not new primary-source research or independent audio analysis. Optional questions invite your response. Thin or ambiguous evidence remains a gap rather than a completed description.

entries.description: Wikipedia connects the writing of “Everything in Its Right Place” to Yorke’s depression during the OK Computer tour and his feeling that he could not speak.
The title track’s melody began with spoken vocals. Wikipedia reports that Yorke’s voice was then vocoded with the ondes Martenot to create the melody.
entries.question: Does knowing that the vocal began as speech change how you follow its melody?

entries.description: “The National Anthem” reaches back to the band’s school years: Wikipedia says Yorke wrote an early version then.

The Orchestra of St John’s performed the strings, recorded in Dorchester Abbey, according to Wikipedia. The account places that session in a twelfth-century church near Radiohead’s Oxfordshire studio.
“Treefingers” was made by digitally processing O’Brien’s guitar loops, according to Wikipedia, which describes the result as an ambient instrumental.
entries.question: Knowing that guitar loops were the starting point, do you hear anything you associate with a guitar, or does the sound suggest something else?

entries.description: Wikipedia traces the refrain of “Optimistic” to reassurance from Yorke’s partner Rachel Owen while he was frustrated with the band’s progress.
A drum-machine pattern made with a modular synthesiser was the starting point for “Idioteque,” according to Wikipedia’s account of Greenwood’s work.
entries.question: How does the rhythmic pattern shape your sense of motion as the track unfolds?

entries.description: Wikipedia draws attention to repeated, contrasting lines in “Morning Bell”: a question about where a car was parked sits against the disturbing instruction to cut the children in half.
entries.question: What effect does the juxtaposition of the everyday and disturbing language have on you?

entries.description: Wikipedia dates the writing of “Motion Picture Soundtrack” to before Radiohead’s debut single “Creep.”
